chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Ali ibn Abi Hamza, who said:

I said to Abu Al-Hasan (peace be upon him): 'A Jew or a Christian had four thousand dirhams in my possession, and he died. Is it permissible for me to reconcile with his heirs without informing them of the exact amount?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'No, until you inform them.'
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on settling with the heirs of a Jew or Christian if you hold their money?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi underscores the principle of *amanah* (trustworthiness) in financial dealings with Ahl al-Kitab, requiring full disclosure of debt amounts before settlement. It highlights the Shia scholarly emphasis on transparency and justice, ensuring that the Muslim creditor does not exploit the non-Muslim heirs' lack of knowledge regarding the exact debt. This ruling reinforces the ethical obligation to treat all parties fairly, regardless of religious difference, in commercial transactions.
